method: docker network disconnect/connect on a dedicated container + volume, three severs of ~20 s (the FREQUENT gap, not the outage), then every ACTIVE harvest the mirror serves cross-checked against pinned eth_call reads. No sudo, no host routing change, structurally unable to reach the launchd kami-lens service or its data dir.

crosscheck.sampling: every ACTIVE harvest on the busiest node (node 86, 1718 rows) plus every 4896th of the remaining 4895, capped at 400. Node-complete is the shape that matters: the 2026-09-06 phantom set was six kamis that stopped in one transaction on one node. Checking all 6613 would be 2x that many pinned eth_calls, which both exceeds any other gate's RPC traffic here and outlasts the RPC's own eth_call state window.
crosscheck.arbitration: the container is live, so a harvest can legitimately stop between the mirror answer and the pinned chain read. Every apparent divergence is re-read from the container afterwards: mirror since corrected = skew; mirror still ACTIVE while the chain says otherwise = a phantom, the 2026-09-06 shape, which persisted for 3.5 hours when it happened.
